Primary drivers include the stable subtropical high-pressure ridge over the eastern Mediterranean, which supports clear skies and light-to-moderate northerly flow. Model guidance shows limited spread, with minimal risk of significant intensification or cooling ahead of the date.

No major synoptic shifts, such as anomalous ridging or enhanced subsidence, have emerged in the latest model runs to push probabilities toward 33°C or higher. Traders appear to weigh these stable atmospheric factors and the narrow forecast window heavily, resulting in concentrated odds around the 31–33°C range while assigning negligible probability to outliers. Model consensus and observational trends show persistent moisture and reduced insolation suppressing peaks, with only modest potential for brief clearing that could allow a 30°C reading. Higher outcomes above 31°C remain low-probability (under 7% combined) given the entrenched rain pattern, while cooler results near 28°C or below reflect downside risks if heavier convection develops. Updated PAGASA and numerical model runs over the next 24 hours will provide the final resolution data for this near-term temperature threshold.
